Read-through with Beige Book context:
- FOMC (May 1): Cautious-hawkish. Activity “solid,” job gains “strong,” but “lack of further progress” on disinflation; cuts on hold until “greater confidence.” QT slowed (Treasury cap to $25B) as a modest risk-management offset.
- SLOOS: Banks continue to tighten C&I and consumer credit with weaker loan demand; CRE standards remain notably tighter. This reinforces that financial conditions are restrictive even without more hikes.
- Beige Book overlay: District reports indicate overall activity expanded since February and firms are optimistic about future growth, with solid convention/tourism in Boston and ongoing labor market strength in New York. At the same time, labor supply has increased and the quality of applicants improved, suggesting some easing in labor-market tightness that could temper wage pressures.

Net tone: Still modestly hawkish due to resilient activity and the FOMC’s “higher-for-longer” stance amid stalled disinflation. However, tighter bank credit and improving labor supply keep the stance close to neutral. On balance, the Beige Book’s evidence of broadening activity and optimism nudges the tone slightly more hawkish than the prior read, but only marginally.
